_comment: Organisations whose own official page does not carry the name this graph uses.
scripts/rename_units_to_official_wording.py is the only writer of these renames;
the curated file is never hand-edited. Every row is re-verified against the live
page on every run -- the table proposes, the page decides -- so a row cannot go
stale silently. CURATION.md records each row, and every proposal refused.
'from' is the name the row was written against: a node that no longer carries it

renames.from: NIST — National Institute of Standards & Technology
renames.to: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
renames.basis: nist.gov is the unit's own site and labels it with this name in page content; the curated name is the same words with the agency's own acronym bolted on in front of an em dash, which is the graph's convention and not anything the page carries.

renames.to: United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
renames.basis: uspto.gov is the office's own site and its masthead reads 'United States Patent and Trademark Office - An Agency of the Department of Commerce', naming the graph's parent for this node as its department. The label sits in the site-wide masthead, so it holds for every page on the host; CLAUDE.md records that as evidence the verifier accepts for an organisation, and the panel says where it sat.

The VA's own page heads this collective 'Veterans Integrated Service Networks' in its content. The curated name states a count — eighteen — that the VA no longer reports, and because it states a count `uncheckable_reason` refuses the name before any fetch, so the node could never earn a source while it was called that. The eighteen numbered networks it carried are marked superseded rather than deleted, and five current ones sit beside them. CURATION.md §10.

A branch of government has no website of its own; usa.gov is the federal government's official portal and its 'Branches of the U.S. government' page is the government's own statement of its structure, labelling all three branches as headings in page content ('Legislative branch', 'Executive branch', 'Judicial branch'). The curated name is the same words with a qualifier bolted on after an em dash, which is the graph's convention and not anything any page carries: canonical_name_key('Legislative Branch — The Congress') is 'legislative branch the congress', and no page labels that, so the top-level node of a whole branch of government could never verify. The Senate Appropriations subcommittee of the same name is not a sibling and is excluded from Treasury name-matching by type; the branch's Treasury line is applied by TREASURY_ROW_ALIASES to the node id, not to the name, and tests/test_treasury_outlays_wiring.py pins that the subcommittee never takes it.
